cards.say: LLMs don't read words. They read **tokens**, small chunks of text. Type below and watch your text split.

props.note: This is a simplified splitter. Real tokenizers differ, but long and rare words do break into more pieces.

cards.q: What does an LLM actually predict?
cards.why: It predicts the most likely next token, adds it, and repeats. Every fluent answer comes from that loop.

cards.say: At every step the model weighs candidate tokens. **Temperature** decides how boldly it picks. Slide it, then sample a few times.

cards.q: You want a contract summary that is steady and repeatable. Which temperature?
cards.why: Low temperature lets the top choice win almost every time, so the same input gives nearly the same output.

cards.q: One sentence in this AI answer is invented. Tap it.
sentences: Photosynthesis turns light, water and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen.
It happens mostly in the chloroplasts of leaf cells.
A 2017 Harvard study by Dr. Elena Marsh proved plants can photosynthesize in total darkness.
cards.why: A name, a year and an institution make it sound solid, but nothing here can be verified, and it contradicts how photosynthesis works. Hallucinations often arrive as confident specifics.

steps: Your prompt is split into tokens
The model scores every possible next token
One token is picked, guided by temperature
The token is added and the loop repeats
cards.why: Split, score, pick, repeat. Each new token becomes part of the input for the next one.
